source: original; stimulus verified against its source (see source_note)

books.section: Western Expansion and Its Impact on the American Character (1860–1895)
Industrialization, Corporate Consolidation, and the Gospel of Wealth

primary_sources: Frederick Jackson Turner, “The Significance of the Frontier in American History,” 1893

stimulus.text: In a recent bulletin of the Superintendent of the Census for 1890 appear these significant words: “Up to and including 1880 the country had a frontier of settlement, but at present the unsettled area has been so broken into by isolated bodies of settlement that there can hardly be said to be a frontier line. In the discussion of its extent, its westward movement, etc., it can not, therefore, any longer have a place in the census reports.” This brief official statement marks the closing of a great historic movement. Up to our own day American history has been in a large degree the history of the colonization of the Great West. The existence of an area of free land, its continuous recession, and the advance of American settlement westward, explain American development.
stimulus.source_note: Frederick Jackson Turner, “The Significance of the Frontier in American History,” 1893, quoting the Superintendent of the Census bulletin for 1890. Public domain; wording and punctuation follow the 1893 Annual Report of the American Historical Association text.

stem: Turner argues that American development came from the frontier experience. Which of the following would most weaken Turner’s argument?

options.text: Settlers on the Plains had to cooperate with neighbors to survive
options.misconception: Cooperation on the frontier still fits a story about frontier life shaping Americans.

options.text: American democracy and self-reliance grew mainly in Eastern cities before western settlement
The census of 1890 found no frontier line
options.misconception: The closed frontier is Turner’s starting point, so it supports him.

options.text: Western settlement spread American institutions across the continent
options.misconception: That is Turner’s own claim, so it supports him.

rationales.A: Hardship and cooperation on the Plains are still frontier experiences.
rationales.B: If the traits came from the East first, the frontier did not create them.
rationales.C: The 1890 census finding is the fact Turner builds on.
rationales.D: Settlement spreading institutions is what Turner argues.
rationales.general:
Ask what would break Turner’s chain.
1. Turner’s claim is that the frontier made American development.
2. A fact that supports him is no help against him.
3. The census finding and the spread of settlement are his own evidence.
4. Only a cause that came before the frontier, in the East, would take the work away from the frontier.
Remember: to weaken a claim, find a different cause for the same result.
